Job Description

About Us

At Thermo Fisher Scientific, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Our Mission is to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. Through our PPD® clinical research services, we support clinical trials in more than 100 countries, delivering laboratory, digital and decentralized solutions that help bring life-changing therapies to patients faster.

Our global Clinical Operations teams provide end-to-end clinical trial support — from study start-up through close-out — across commercial and government-sponsored studies.

Why Join Thermo Fisher Scientific / PPD?

- Work on high-quality, global clinical trials across diverse therapeutic areas
- Be part of a stable, well-established organization with long-term career opportunities
- Strong collaboration with experienced CTMs and project teams
- Clear development pathways (e.g., Senior CRA, Lead CRA, CTM)
- Flexible working models that support work-life balance
- Permanent employment
- Full-time (40 hours/week) or Part-time (32 hours/week) options available

About the Role

This position is for experienced Clinical Research Associates with 2+ years of independent monitoring experience. You will manage clinical trial sites across Germany, ensuring studies are conducted in compliance with the protocol, ICH-GCP, applicable regulations, and company SOPs.

You’ll work autonomously, partner closely with investigative sites, and collaborate with project teams to deliver high-quality, inspection-ready clinical trials.

What You’ll Do

- Perform site monitoring activities (on-site and remote) using a risk-based monitoring approach
- Ensure protocol, ICH-GCP, regulatory, and SOP compliance at investigator sites
- Conduct SDR, SDV, CRF review, and investigational product accountability
- Identify, document, escalate, and follow up on issues through resolution, applying root cause analysis and CAPA principles
- Maintain audit and inspection readiness at all assigned sites
- Build strong, collaborative relationships with investigators and site staff
- Document monitoring activities in timely, high-quality reports and follow-up letters
- Maintain ongoing communication with sites between visits to support issue resolution and data quality
- Ensure study systems (e.g., CTMS) are updated according to study conventions
- Provide trial status updates and metrics to the Clinical Team Manager (CTM)
- Support study start-up, investigator identification, site initiation, and study close-out activities as assigned
- Participate in investigator meetings, audits, inspections, and project team meetings as required

Additional responsibilities may include supporting process improvement initiatives, mentoring activities, or project-specific tasks aligned with experience.

A Day in the Life

- Review site metrics and prioritize monitoring activities based on risk
- Conduct on-site or remote monitoring visits
- Partner with sites to resolve findings and improve processes
- Collaborate with CTMs and project teams to keep studies on track and inspection-ready
- Complete documentation, system updates, and administrative tasks

Education & Experience

- Bachelor’s degree in a life sciences related field or equivalent qualification
- Minimum 2+ years of experience as a Clinical Research Associate / Monitor
- Valid driver’s license
- Full right to work in Germany
- Fluency in German and English (C1 level) – interviews will be conducted in German

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

- Strong clinical monitoring skills with hands-on RBM experience
- Excellent understanding and application of ICH-GCP and applicable regulations
- Solid therapeutic area knowledge and medical terminology
- Well-developed critical thinking, problem-solving, and root cause analysis skills
- Strong written and verbal communication skills with medical professionals
- High attention to detail and strong organizational skills
- Ability to work independently while contributing effectively to cross-functional teams
- Flexibility and adaptability in a dynamic project environment
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office and ability to learn clinical systems (e.g., CTMS)

Locations: Home-based or hybrid anywhere in Germany
FTE: Full-time (40 hrs/week) or Part-time 80% (32 hrs/week)
Contract: Permanent
Travel: Approximately 50–75% (study-dependent)

Keysight (https://www.keysight.com/us/en/about.html)  is on the forefront of technology innovation, delivering breakthroughs and trusted insights in electronic design, simulation, prototyping, test, manufacturing, and optimization. Our ~15,000 employees create world-class solutions in communications, 5G, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace, defense, and semiconductor markets for customers in over 100 countries. Learn more about what we do. (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ykxkSz5DlPo&t=16s)

Our award-winning (https://jobs.keysight.com/awards)  culture embraces a bold vision of where technology can take us and a passion for tackling challenging problems with industry-first solutions. We believe that when people feel a sense of belonging, they can be more creative, innovative, and thrive at all points in their careers.

About the Role
In this hybrid role combining UI expertise with broader software engineering, you’ll contribute to the development of next-generation simulation applications that integrate real-world physics, interactive visualization, and responsive user interfaces.

As a UI Software Engineer – Simulation Applications, you won’t just focus on aesthetic frontend components—you’ll work across the presentation and application layers, contributing to the overall architecture, functional behavior, and user experience of complex engineering tools. This includes enabling seamless data interaction, responsive controls for simulation parameters, and integration of real-time results.

Your work will directly impact how engineers across domains interact with simulation environments that support their product innovation and validation.

About the Team

Join a collaborative and international R&D team based in Frankfurt, working closely with colleagues in the USA and other global locations. You’ll be part of an agile group of frontend developers and UX designers, backed by experienced software architects and domain experts in physics and mathematics.

Responsibilities

- Collaborate with product managers and UX designers to translate user needs into intuitive UI features.
- Develop and design new software features for our engineering applications to meet key market and next-generation product goals.
- Maintain and enhance existing applications.
- Ensure high-quality code with automated testing and documentation.
- Contribute to code reviews and continuous integration processes.

Required Qualifications

- Solid experience with C++ and object-oriented software design.

Desired Qualifications

- In general, a hybrid model with on-site presence 2–3 days every other week or every 2nd week is expected.

We value flexibility and trust our teams to coordinate in a way that supports both individual needs and team effectiveness.

You develop and operate the test infrastructure for our aerospace components — from test method and test bench design to campaign execution, data evaluation, and traceable reporting. You bring a fresh engineering perspective to new projects and strengthen our validation capabilities with every campaign.

THE WHY
To end COPV failure in spaceflight.
Every composite pressure vessel that flies is proven on a test bench first. Testing is where design assumptions meet physical reality — burst, proof, cycle, and environmental campaigns generate the data that lets our customers trust their hardware in orbit. This role owns that proof.

YOUR IMPACT

You don't run tests. You deliver proof.

You ensure:
• every test campaign delivers reliable, reproducible data on schedule
• test benches and methods evolve with our products — not behind them
• results are documented so clearly that anyone can trace a data point back to its source

Important note: This role covers hardware testing and quality assurance of our COPVs and carbon structures. We are not hiring for Software QA or software testing positions.

Your tasks in detail and by priority:

Provide test infrastructure
Develop, build, and technically provision test methods and test benches — mechanical, hydraulic, and pneumatic setups including sensor and DAQ integration — to support product validation and qualification.
→ High Performance: Precision at speed. Test-ready when the hardware is.

Plan and execute test campaigns
Conceptualize, prepare, and run structured test campaigns (e.g. proof, burst, pressure cycling, or environmental testing) according to project and customer requirements. You own the campaign end-to-end.
→ Accountability: Your bench, your campaign, your data.

Evaluate measurement data and report with precision
Analyze measurement results, assess accuracy and reliability, and prepare comprehensive and fully traceable test reports. The data says what it says — you report it straight.
→ Candor: Honest data. Clear reports. No spin.

Drive engineering solutions
Approach testing challenges with curiosity and initiative — new fixtures, smarter instrumentation, and better methods. Testing is applied problem-solving, and you treat it that way.
→ Playfulness: Experiment on the bench, not in production.

Collaborate on-site
Work hands-on with design, manufacturing, and quality teams in Taufkirchen to close the loop between test results and product improvement.
→ Togetherness: Test data only matters if the whole team can act on it.

• First practical experience (internships, thesis projects, or 1-3 years of professional experience) in hardware testing, test bench development, or an experimental engineering environment.

• Strong ownership mindset and the ability to drive technical topics forward in a structured and independent manner.
• Fluent English and a curious, hands-on mindset with a strong willingness to learn.

Nice to have
• Experience with composite materials or pressure vessel testing.
• Experience with LabVIEW, aerospace testing standards (e.g. ECSS), cryogenic testing, or measurement uncertainty analysis.

• High level of autonomy & real impact: You own a critical seam in the business — between what we sell and what we build

jobs.description:
The German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ) is one of Europe’s largest cancer research centers. “Research for a life without cancer" is the mission of our world-class scientists and all our team members.

The DKFZ is a place where the brightest minds pursue bold ideas and seek answers to pioneering scientific questions through collaboration, innovation, and exploration across many disciplines. We provide a dynamic environment which empowers excellence with state-of-the-art technologies, cutting edge infrastructure, and a global scientific network. 

Contribute your knowledge, vision, and dedication to create a space where scientific discovery in cancer research is transformed into benefits for human health.

For our Junior Research Group Pediatric Immuno-Oncology (led by Dr. Dr. Franziska Blaeschke) we are seeking, starting in January 2027, a PhD Student - Immunotherapy/Optical CRISPR Screens/Spatial Transcriptomics.

Our group uses advanced genetic engineering and high-throughput CRISPR screens to improve CAR- and TCR-based immunotherapies. This project explores how highly effective anti-tumor immune cells can be identified and enhanced to better fight cancer. By combining functional screening (e.g., genome-wide CRISPR screens), cutting-edge cell engineering (e.g., AAV-based knockins, base editing), and innovative imaging and sequencing technologies (e.g., NIS-seq, spatial transcriptomics/proteomics), we aim to uncover key features of the most powerful anti-tumor T cells (“elite” immune cells) and translate these insights into next-generation immunotherapies.
The work will include a large variety of experimental methods and models (in vitro and in vivo), in close collaboration with the groups of Prof. Dr. Adelheid Cerwenka (Department of Immunobiochemistry, Medical Faculty Mannheim of Heidelberg University), Prof. Dr. Joachim Spatz (Department of Cellular Biophysics, Max Planck Institute), Prof. Dr. Nina Papavasiliou (Division of Immune Diversity, DKFZ), Prof. Dr. Michael Platten (Clinical Cooperation Unit Neuroimmunology and Brain Tumor Immunology at DKFZ and Department of Neurology at the University Medical Center Mannheim), and Dr. Vibor Laketa (Infectious Diseases Imaging Platform, UKHD). Together, the project seeks to define and build next-generation immune cells with enhanced therapeutic potential.

Your Tasks

- Establishing new experimental protocols and optimizing technologies (e.g., NIS-seq, spatial CRISPR screens)
- Working on computational approaches to read out CRISPR screens, imaging and sequencing data (e.g., spatial transcriptomics/proteomics)
- Designing and performing complex experiments involving a large number of methods (e.g., cloning, CRISPR/Cas9, viral transduction, AAV generation, flow cytometry, microfluidics systems, next-generation sequencing, microscopy, xenograft and syngeneic models, primary cell culture, functional analyses such as cytokine release, proliferation, cytotoxicity assays etc.)
- Staying up to date with scientific literaturePresenting your research on a regular basis within the group, the DKFZ/KiTZ and externally
- Preparing grants, patents, and publications

Your Profile

- Completed studies with a diploma or master's degree in biology, bioengineering, biomedical science, biochemistry, bioinformatics, or other relevant fields

A Snapshot of Your Day 

As a Resident Quality Engineer (f/m/d), you will spend your day working closely with suppliers, manufacturing teams, and cross-functional stakeholders to ensure product quality, production stability, and delivery performance. A significant portion of your role involves being on-site at supplier locations, leading quality escalations, supporting production recovery, and driving sustainable process improvements. You will analyze manufacturing challenges, coordinate corrective actions, conduct audits, and collaborate with engineering and operations teams to strengthen process capability and customer satisfaction. With approximately 25–30% travel, you will play a critical role in maintaining quality excellence across the supply chain.

How You’ll Make an Impact 

* Deployment to supplier sites as a dedicated quality escalation expert to stabilize production following critical quality, technical, or delivery issues
* Leadership of immediate containment activities to prevent defect escapes, protect customers, and maintain operational continuity
* Development and management of supplier recovery plans including action tracking, milestone management, accountability, and executive reporting
* Execution of root cause analyses, manufacturing process reviews, and quality audits to identify risks, process gaps, and improvement opportunities
* Definition, implementation, validation, and sustainability tracking of corrective and preventive actions to address both short-term and systemic issues
* Collaboration with supplier engineering, quality, and operations teams to improve process capability, product quality, manufacturing efficiency, and long-term performance

What You Bring

* Bachelor’s or master’s degree in Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Quality Engineering, or a related technical discipline
* Extensive experience in quality management, manufacturing environments, supplier quality, and production process improvement
* Strong expertise in root cause analysis, problem-solving methodologies, Kaizen, supplier recovery activities, and critical manufacturing process assessments
* Proven ability to identify technical failure mechanisms, implement sustainable process improvements, and ensure long-term effectiveness of corrective actions
* Experience working in cross-functional and international environments, ideally with turbine hot gas components or other complex manufacturing technologies
* Strong communication, stakeholder management, and analytical skills, combined with fluency in German and English and willingness to travel approximately 25–30% to supplier locations worldwide

Our Gas Services division offers Low-emission power generation through service and

At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100.000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation.

Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.
